page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core CPU stress tests, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall within the average range. Memory performance is notable, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%, while raw memory bandwidth read and write operations remain average. For language model tasks, text generation using a small 135M parameter model achieves strong performance in the top 25%, whereas larger 7B model inference speeds align with average tiers.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, this server offers balanced resource density for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. The inclusion of a 1600 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-capacity, low-latency storage directly bundled with the compute resources. This configuration is well-suited for database hosting, redis caching layers, memory-bound data processing, and moderate-scale web serving workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU execution and a large memory footprint.
description: The Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high 8.0 GB per core ratio, and includes a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong memory scores, alongside average multi-core and database execution capabilities. Lacking a GPU, it relies on its dedicated CPU allocation and substantial memory capacity to deliver stable performance. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and caching layers that require a balance of dedicated compute and high-capacity local NVMe storage.
